full_judgment: 13. In fact that was a caution of the highest Court to the High Court Division regarding the scope of such extra-ordinary discretion. While considering an application for anticipatory bail under section 498 (Old) of the Code in the case of State vs Captain Jagit Singh AIR 1962 SC 253 it was held by the Supreme Court of India that, "It is of paramount consideration to remember that the freedom of the individual is as necessary for the survival of the society as it is for the egoistic purposes of the individual. A person seeking anticipatory bail is still a free man entitled to the presumption of innocence. He is willing to submit to restraint on his freedom, by the acceptance on conditions which the Court may think fit to impose, in consideration of the assurance that if arrested, he shall be enlarged on bail. In Salahuddin Abdul Samad Sheikh's case Indian Supreme Court held that, "Ordinarily the Court granting anticipatory bail should not substitute itself for the original Court which is expected to deal with the offence. It is that Court which has then to consider whether, having regard to the material placed before it, the accused person is entitled to bail."
